192: KATERINA. A vow that I will not dare while you're away on any ground whatever to speak with any outsider, nor see anyone,—that I will not even dare to think of anyone but you. KABANOV. But what's this for?
190: KABANOV. Now, come, I can't, so it's no use. KATERINA. Well, here then! Take from me some dreadful vow....
189: KATERINA. Tisha, what are you leaving me to? There'll be trouble when you're away! There'll be trouble!
187: KABANOV. I can't make you out, Katia! Often there's no getting a word out of you, to say nothing of a kiss, and now you come coaxing up to me of your own accord.
185: KATERINA ( goes up to her husband and draws him to her ). Tisha, dear one, if you would stay, if you would take me with you, how I would love you, how I would cherish you, my dear one!
182: KABANOV. Say things? Why, what things am I to say? God knows what it is you're afraid of! You won't be alone, you know, you'll be with mamma. KATERINA. Don't speak of her, don't torture my heart! Ah, how wretched I am, how wretched! ( Weeps .) Where can I go? Whom can I cling to? Merciful Heavens, I am lost!
180: KATERINA. How can I care for you, when you say things like that?
179: KATERINA. Why, can it be that you are tired of me?
177: KABANOV. Much fun there would be in going with you! You've worried me out of my life here between you! No sooner have I a hope of escaping than you want to fasten yourself upon me.
175: KABANOV ( freeing himself from her embrace ). But it's impossible!
174: KATERINA. Well, take me with you, do take me!
172: KABANOV. I must, Katia. When mamma sends me, how can I not go?
171: KATERINA ( still in the same position, slightly shaking her head ). Peace be with you! ( Hiding her face in her hands ) She has hurt me! KABANOV. If you take everything to heart so, you'll soon fall into a decline. Why listen to her! You know she must talk! Well then, let her talk, and you let it go in at one ear and out at the other. Come, good-bye, Katia!
169: KABANOV. But why are you like this? Come, forgive me!
168: KATERINA ( after a protracted silence—shakes her head ). No!
167: MME. KABANOVA. Well, now you can talk by yourselves a little, if you want to. Come, Varvara! [ They go out . KABANOV. Katia! ( Silence .) Katia, you're not angry with me?
165: MME. KABANOVA ( severely ). Enough of this nonsense! It's your duty to do what your mother tells you. ( With a smile ) It's always as well when it's forbidden.
163: KABANOV. But that is too much, mamma, for mercy's sake!
161: MME. KABANOVA. Not to stare at young fellows while you are away!
160: KABANOV. Don't look out of window!
157: KABANOV. But, mamma, whenever has she....
156: MME. KABANOVA. Not to go staring out of window!
155: KABANOV. Do some work while I am away!
153: MME. KABANOVA. Not to sit with her hands in her lap like a fine lady.
152: KABANOV. Revere mamma, Katia, as your own mother.
151: KABANOV. Don't be saucy! MME. KABANOVA. To revere her mother-in-law as her own mother.
150: MME. KABANOVA. Tell her not to be saucy to her mother-in-law.
148: KABANOV ( standing opposite Katerina ). Obey mamma, Katia.
146: MME. KABANOVA. The way you talk! Come, come, give your commands, that I may hear what commands you lay upon her! And then when you come back, you can ask if she has performed everything exactly.
145: [ Katerina looks on the ground . KABANOV. But she knows quite well without that.
143: MME. KABANOVA. Why are you standing about? Don't you know the way to do things? Lay your commands upon your wife, exhort her how she is to live in your absence.
142: MME. KABANOVA. Well? KABANOV. What do you desire?
141: MME. KABANOVA. Well, now everything is ready. The horses are at the door. You've only to say good-bye and be off in God's name. KABANOV. Yes, mamma, it's time I was off.
139: [ Enter Mme. Kabanova and Kabanov . MME. KABANOVA. Now do you remember everything I've told you? Mind you do remember it! Keep it in your heart!
138: VARVARA. Bound! Oh, will he! As soon as he gets away, he'll start drinking, you may be sure. He says nothing now, but all the while he's only thinking how to get away as soon as possible.
137: KATERINA. And so even when he's free he'll be as good as bound.
135: VARVARA. For nothing at all, teaching him to mind what he's about. He'll be a fortnight away out of her sight! Only fancy! She has an uneasy inkling all the time that he'll enjoy himself when he's his own master. And so she's busy now laying all sorts of injunctions upon him, each more imperative than the last, and then she'll take him up to the holy picture and make him swear solemnly that he'll do everything exactly and precisely according to her bidding.
134: VARVARA. He's sitting locked up with mamma. She's nagging away at him now. KATERINA. What for?
132: KATERINA. No, I only wondered, he has to start so soon.
131: VARVARA. Why, do you want him?
130: [ Silence . KATERINA. Where can Tihon be?
129: KATERINA. You must be joking. VARVARA. To be sure, I am joking; did you think I meant it?
128: KATERINA ( looking at her ). What for? VARVARA.( laughing ). We'll tell our fortunes together there.
127: VARVARA. I wouldn't have asked you, only mamma wouldn't let me alone, and I must.
126: KATERINA. Still one feels nervous, somehow! But perhaps I will.
125: VARVARA. Timid, nonsense! Glasha will be with us.
123: KATERINA. I'm timid of sleeping in a place I'm not used to.
121: VARVARA. Why, isn't it just the same to you?
117: VARVARA. Do you know what, Katia! When Tihon's gone, let's sleep in the garden, in the summerhouse.
115: KATERINA. Ah, Varia, you don't know me! I pray, of course, it may never come to that! But if I am too miserable here, they would not keep me by any force on earth. I should throw myself out of the window, I should drown myself in the Volga. If I will not to live here, then I would not, they might cut me to pieces! ( Silence. )
114: VARVARA. Where would you go? You are a married woman.
112: KATERINA. What do I care! I should go away, and that would be the end of it.
110: VARVARA. Just try; why they'd torment you to death.
109: KATERINA. Whatever I long to do, I will do.
108: VARVARA. Yes, what will you do?
104: VARVARA. And when you can't bear it, what will you do?
102: KATERINA. I don't like that. What good can come of it! I had much better bear it as long as I can bear it.
101: VARVARA. You are such a fantastical creature, God bless you! What I think is: one should do what one likes, only be sure it's kept dark!
99: VARVARA. All right, don't think of him; no one compels you to.
97: KATERINA. Don't speak to me of him, for goodness' sake, don't speak of him! I don't want to know him even. I will love my husband: Tisha, my dear one, no one shall ever take your place! I did not want to think of him, you tempt me.
95: VARVARA. He is so sad and unhappy....
93: KATERINA ( her head still more bent down ). As if we could meet! And what would be the use....
92: VARVARA. He sent greetings to you. He was sorry, he said, that he never meets you.
90: KATERINA ( after a short silence, looking down ). Well?
88: VARVARA. But there's no doing without deceit; think where you're living! Our whole house rests on it! I wasn't fond of lying either, but I learnt the trick, when I had to. I was out walking yesterday, and so I saw him and had a few minutes talk with him.
87: KATERINA. I can't deceive, I don't know how to conceal anything.
86: KATERINA. Yes, yes, Varia! Only mind, Varia, for pity's sake.... VARVARA. What nonsense! You'd better mind, and not betray yourself in any way.
84: VARVARA. Why, you know, what's the use of telling his name? KATERINA. No, tell it! Tell his name!
82: KATERINA ( still looking down ). Well, whom then?
80: KATERINA ( with dismay ). How did you notice it?
78: VARVARA. Oh, no, you don't. If you're sorry for him you don't love him. And indeed you've no great reason to, I must own. And it's no good your being so close with me! I noticed a long while ago, that you were fond of some one.
77: KATERINA. Oh, yes, I do! I'm dreadfully sorry for him.
76: VARVARA. And you know, Katia, you don't love Tihon.
75: KATERINA. No, I only laughed at them.
73: VARVARA. Well? And didn't you care for anyone?
70: VARVARA. Really! And were there any men in love with you, as a girl?
69: VARVARA. Why? KATERINA. I have been like that from my birth up, full of fire! I was only six years old, when do you know what I did? They offended me somehow at home,—it was in the evening and quite dark—I ran away to the Volga, and got into a boat, and pushed it off from the bank. They found me next morning, ten miles down the river.
68: [ Glasha goes out. KATERINA. And it always will be.
65: FEKLUSHA. For their infidelity. I am going off on my rounds among the merchant gentry, my dear, to see if there won't be some alms for poverty. Good-bye for the present!
63: GLASHA. How do they come to have dogs' heads?
62: GLASHA. And have you travelled far in your wanderings, Feklusha?
60: FEKLUSHA. Ah, my good girl, that comes of the hatred the evil one has for us, because we lead a life of such holiness. But I can't say, my dear, that I'm one to gossip; that's not a sin of mine. One failing I have, truly; I know myself what it is. I love dainty eating. Well, well, the Lord in His mercy provides according to my weakness.
59: FEKLUSHA. One can't be without sin, my good girl; we live in the world. I'll tell you what, my dear; you, simple folk, are tempted of one devil, but we pilgrim folk are beset, one with six, another with twelve devils; and here we have to struggle against all at once. It's a hard fight, my dear, a hard fight! GLASHA. Why is it you have such a lot?
57: FEKLUSHA. Well now, my dear, if there's one thing I love, it's to hear a wail well done! ( Silence. ) And mind you keep a sharp look out, my girl, on the beggar woman below, that she don't lay her hands on anything.
56: GLASHA. Never heard of her doing it.
55: GLASHA. That I can't say, really. FEKLUSHA. But she does wail at times, I suppose?
53: FEKLUSHA. Well, God speed him on his way! And say, will the young mistress do a wail for his going or not?
52: FEKLUSHA. Is he going to be away long, my dear? GLASHA. No, not long.
51: FEKLUSHA. Is he going away then—the light of our eyes? GLASHA. Yes.
50: GLASHA. I'm getting the master's things ready for his journey.
49: Enter FEKLUSHA. FEKLUSHA. Dear girl, always at work! What are you doing, my dear?
48: GLASHA ( packing up clothes in a bundle ).
47: [ Thunder. KATERINA. Ah! Make haste! Make haste!
46: [ Enter Kabanov. VARVARA. Here comes my brother. ( To Kabanov ) Hurry up!
44: VARVARA. I didn't know you were so afraid of a thunderstorm. I'm not afraid, you see.
43: KATERINA. No, but still, it's better there, it's quieter; at home one can turn to the holy pictures and pray to God!
42: VARVARA. But if anything were to happen, you know, you'd be no safer at home.
41: VARVARA. But why are you so awfully frightened? The storm's a long way off yet. KATERINA. If it's so far off, we'll wait then a little, if you like; but really it would be better to go. Yes, we'd better go home.
40: KATERINA. No, let us go home! Never mind him!
38: VARVARA. Why, are you crazy? How can you show yourself at home without my brother?
37: KATERINA ( in terror ). A storm! Let us run home! Make haste!
35: VARVARA ( looking round ). I say, brother doesn't come, and yonder there's a storm coming up.
33: KATERINA. I am afraid, terribly afraid! I seem to see her all the while before us. [ Silence.
31: VARVARA. There's nothing to be frightened of! An old fool....
29: KATERINA ( shrinking ). Ah, ah, stop! I can't bear it!
27: KATERINA. What was it she said, eh? what did she say?
25: VARVARA. Her curse fall on her own head, the old witch!
23: KATERINA. Ah, how she frightened me! I'm trembling all over, as if she were foretelling something for me.
20: OLD LADY. Hey, my pretty charmers? What are you doing here? Waiting for young fellows, waiting for your beaus? Are your hearts merry? Merry are they? Are you pleased and proud of your beauty? That's where beauty leads to. ( Points to the Volga ) Yes, yes, to the bottomless pit! ( Varvara smiles. ) What, laughing? Let not your heart rejoice! ( Knocks with her stick ) You will burn all of you in a fire unquenchable. You will boil in the lake of flaming pitch. ( Going ) That is whither beauty leads you!
19: VARVARA. Why wear yourself out for nothing? You may die of grieving, do you suppose they'll be sorry for you? Come, wait a bit. Why, what's the good of making yourself miserable? [ Enter the Old Lady with a stick and two footmen in three-cornered hats behind her.
18: KATERINA. No, no, don't talk to me, I don't want to hear!
17: VARVARA. Oh well, wait a little, and then we shall see.
16: VARVARA. Why are you frightened? KATERINA. If I were once to see and speak with him, I should run away from home, I would not go back home for anything in the world.
14: KATERINA. No, no, that must not be! What are you saying! God forbid!
12: VARVARA. Mercy on us! what is coming to you! Come, wait a bit, brother's going away to-morrow, we'll think of something; maybe, you'll be able to see each other.
10: KATERINA. What am I to do? I'm at the end of my strength, where can I find help. I'm so wretched, I shall do something dreadful.
8: VARVARA. I'm not likely to be hard upon you! I've sins enough of my own.
7: VARVARA. As if I didn't know!
5: KATERINA. How do you know that?
4: VARVARA. But not with your husband.
2: VARVARA. You've no need! Tell away.
0: KATERINA. Oh what am I to tell you? I'm ashamed.
